title: A SEMANTIC-GATE REFUSAL IS BYPASSABLE: THE ESCALATION PATH LANDS A PATCH THE GATE REJECTED, ON TYPECHECK ALONE. MEASURED
description: A SEMANTIC-GATE REFUSAL IS BYPASSABLE: THE ESCALATION PATH LANDS A PATCH THE GATE REJECTED, ON TYPECHECK ALONE. MEASURED 2026-09-05, dispatch de562190-6671-4799-9a38-28175693c05b against repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/rhythm-conductor-tick.ts. feature_compose returned verdict=UNFAVORABLE and rolled back, with the semantic gate reporting 'adversarial refuters agreed 2/2 (conf 1.00, 0.90): DESTROY-TO-SATISFY'. The same run then reports: 'escalated to patch_with_tools which committed/pushed a typecheck-verified patch ... to origin/dev'. Commit 0191cbd landed and the change is present in the deployed file and in the running process (unit ActiveEnterTimestamp 08:28:21 follows the commit at 08:27:43). SO THE SEMANTIC GATE IS NOT A STOP. A patch two independent refuters rejected at confidence 1.00 reached origin/dev through a second exit path whose stated verification is TYPECHECK ONLY. The gate governs the feature_compose lane; the escalation lane does not appear to re-run it. THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS A KNOWN GAP — a landing check that covers one of several exit paths. The verification chain is only as strong as its weakest exit, and escalation is currently the weakest. IMPORTANT AND SEPARATE: ON THIS OCCASION THE GATE WAS WRONG AND THE LANDED PATCH IS CORRECT. The change adds regResp !== null to the emit guard so a failed or timed-out registry read cannot file a false registry_empty gap. Verified by executing the deployed condition across five cases: a failed read goes from emitting to not emitting; a GENUINELY empty registry STILL emits (so nothing was destroyed to satisfy the goal); the unmappable break, the healthy case and dry-run are all unchanged. The refuters' concern — that one can satisfy 'do not emit wrongly' by simply not emitting — is reasonable in form and false on these facts. That the gate can be both wrong AND bypassed is precisely why the bypass matters: the next patch it refuses may deserve the refusal. FALSIFIER: closed only when a patch the semantic gate refuses is shown NOT to reach origin/dev by any path, or the escalation path is shown to run the same semantic gate — cite a refused patch and the exit paths tested. A closure that only re-states typecheck coverage is fabricated.
